scope: Theorem 4.1 (Balanced three-stack realization) of the manuscript “Incompressible Box Transport and Finite Computation” (preprints/Incompressible-Box-Transport-and-Finite-Computation-October-6-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2505dc09d3f2c24b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every machine and finite input, there are effective coefficients f0, f1 such that f = f0 + νf1 on R3 has an explicit zero-data solution (U, 0). Force and velocity have one compact spatial support and bounded mixed derivatives of every order, and are one-periodic after t = 1. At the fixed label x∗ = (4, 0, 0), ∃t ≥ 0 : X(t; x∗) ∈ (−1, 2)3 ⇐⇒ the machine halts. For a fixed machine its repeated field is independent of the input. The comparison class is u ∈ CH2 ∩ C1L2, bounded u, ∇u on finite intervals, and pressure modulo constants in CH1. The formula is valid for every fixed real ν > 0, with effective evaluation when ν is computable and relative evaluation otherwise.
